findings.summary: T-01, T-02 and T-03 all simulate clean against the real tree in both Git Bash and PowerShell 7. The sha256 pin prints 9ae7045f6b73c4259c38ded17d5026f01da981e5b7a14ee7b48ec40297a72ebc in both shells; all five T-02 checks reproduce their stated values exactly, including the 5 files / 83 insertions / 15 deletions diffstat and its five pre-declared CRLF warnings; the pathspec magic ':(exclude)changes' survives PowerShell quoting, which was round 2's C1 failure mode; git diff --cached --stat is empty so the index equals HEAD today; -uall invariance holds for checks (a) and (c). The AC-03 probe is byte-identical in both shells and the AC-01 baseline reproduces (pass 1 / fail 1, SyntaxError at test/high.test.mjs:15:25). All eight runtime-plugin citations are accurate to the line.

CONFIRMED as stated: design.md:309-310 and :417-418 assert no AC-02 check reads changes/high/, but check (e) reads changes/high/specs/cli-output/spec.md. The premise is false and both conclusions survive; the 'unmonitored' reading is contradicted three times in the same file (design.md:242, :405, tasks.md:13(e)) and T-02 names check (e) inline, so an executor cannot reach the wrong behavior from it.

Mechanism CONFIRMED, executability impact REFUTED. git diff --stat is index-relative and porcelain's two-column code is index-sensitive, but nothing in tasks.md, acceptance.md or design.md instructs a git add or a commit, the index is empty, and all four expected values reproduce as written. The residual is narrower than the architect framed it: check (e) is content-based and immune, (a)/(b) flip only if the executor stages its own file, and a commit scoped to changes/high leaves (d) intact - only a commit that sweeps in changes/medium (git add -A, git commit -am) empties (d) and triggers the false accusation at acceptance.md:99-101. 'git diff --stat HEAD -- changes/medium' returns the identical stat, so the architect's fix is correct and free, but it is hardening rather than a prerequisite.

CONFIRMED, and it opened no hole. The deleted machinery was no better: design.md:226 already concedes the baseline could not detect a content change inside a collapsed untracked directory nor a further edit to an already-modified file under changes/medium/. The only shape the old baseline caught that (d) misses is a new untracked file directly under changes/medium/, which makes design.md:240-241's 'strictly stronger' a slight overclaim rather than a regression. The gate still catches the shape that matters: an edit to test/high.test.mjs trips both (a) and (b).

CONFIRMED, trivially non-blocking. design.md:363's coverage claim is open at the edges (.git/ lands in no group either) but check (a) catches any new root-level file regardless. With core.autocrlf=true and cli.mjs LF-terminated, check (b) will most likely emit its own CRLF warning post-edit, naming only cli.mjs, so both the literal and intended readings still pass.

Explicit judgement: W1-W5 do not justify ending planning unapproved. They are defects of prose about the gate, not of the gate; all three tasks executed against the real tree without inventing a single rule, command, expected value or decision. Rounds 1 and 2 rejected because T-02 named no runnable comparison command and because AC-02's baseline machinery went red on a byte-identical implementation - those made the plan unexecutable. Any edit made to satisfy W1-W5 would invalidate R-8's WATCH and demand a re-review this budget cannot fund.
